item.title: Absolute Calibration of a Broadband Transmission Grating Spectrometer from 5 to 400 nm with Uncertainty Estimates
item.description: arXiv:2611.09288v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present the absolute calibration of a transmission grating spectrometer (TGS) with uncertainty estimates in the 5--400 nm range using synchrotron radiation at the BEAR beamline at Elettra light source in Trieste, Italy. Firstly, the spectral responsivity of a Si photodiode in the spectrometer was absolutely calibrated with respect to the absolutely-calibrated beamline photodiode. Subsequently, this photodiode was used to calibrate the transmittance of Zr and Al thin-film filters, along with bulk MgF$_2$ and UV-grade fused silica windows at their operating positions in the spectrometer to minimize mounting-induced uncertainties. Next, the quantum efficiency of the spectrometer's CCD camera was calibrated over the 5--400 nm range. Lastly, three gratings with line densities of 10000, 3000, and 1000 lines/mm were calibrated for spectroscopy in the ranges extending from soft X-ray to extreme-, vacuum- and deep-ultraviolet (DUV) wavelengths, respectively. The combination of various filters and gratings enables absolutely calibrated spectroscopy with high versatility across a broad wavelength range from soft X-rays to DUV.
item.dc:creator: E. Chebykin, A. E. H. Gaballah, R. van der Horst, A. Giglia, N. Mahne, M. van de Kerkhof, M. D. Ackermann, M. Bayraktar

item.title: A State-Variable Theory of Evolving Material Symmetry
item.description: arXiv:2611.09314v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Material architecture can evolve during loading, yet its mechanically expressed symmetry depends on both the structural state and the constitutive coupling. We connect these quantities through one parent-invariant free energy with a symmetric traceless internal tensor $\mathbf Q$. Its stabilizer distinguishes isotropic, uniaxial, and biaxial states, and projected gradient kinetics satisfies the structural dissipation inequality. Parent invariance generally guarantees only symmetry inheritance. For an explicit two-coupling elastic potential, we derive a stiffness-contraction reconstruction of $\mathbf Q$ and prove equality of the structural and tangent rotational symmetries for every nonzero coupling pair. The associated acoustic tensor links residual symmetry to protected transverse degeneracies. For a small uniaxial state, the leading squared-speed gap is $|\gamma_2s|\sin^2\vartheta/(2\rho_0)$; coupling selectivity and residual protection can suppress this term. We also derive a directional acoustic-trace reconstruction and state calibrated and nuisance-aware inverse conditions. Dimensionless structural-field, acoustic, transient finite-element, and synthetic inverse examples illustrate the predictions. The framework connects state evolution, mechanically expressed symmetry, and conditional observability without assigning independent dynamics to a group label.
item.dc:creator: Pengfei Zhu, Leiming Du, Guoqi Zhang

item.title: Spin to Orbital Angular Momentum Conversion in the Neutron Nucleus Weak Interaction
item.description: arXiv:2611.09677v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The neutron nucleus weak interaction generates a small parity non conserving rotation of the neutron spin as the neutron moves through matter. This parity-odd neutron rotary power can reach up to 2.2e-3 rad * cm-1 for slow neutrons in 139La, which possesses a p-wave resonance at 0.7 eV where the parity-odd asymmetry is greatly amplified. This spin rotation must conserve total angular momentum. Here we show that this conservation occurs through neutron orbital angular momentum generation. We experimentally demonstrate that a neutron prepared initially in a longitudinal spin-orbit state experiences no change in total angular momentum.
item.dc:creator: Niels Geerits, Stephan Sponar, Hartmut Lemmel, Andrea Piovano, Kyle Steffen, William Michael Snow

item.title: Experimental demonstration of dual-polarization nonreciprocal thermal emission at moderate magnetic fields
item.description: arXiv:2611.07564v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Conventional thermal emitters obey Kirchhoff's law of thermal radiation, which requires emissivity and absorptivity to be equal at each wavelength, angle, and polarization. This in turn places a fundamental limit on a range of radiative energy technologies as well as heat transfer. This constraint can however be overcome using magneto-optic semiconductors, which break Lorentz reciprocity under an applied magnetic field. However, in most prior experimental demonstrations, nonreciprocity has been restricted to TM polarization, since the electric field of TE-polarized light is parallel to the applied magnetic field. Here, we experimentally demonstrate nonreciprocal absorption in both polarizations at the same wavelengths and angles from a single structure, wherein a germanium Mie-resonant metasurface on a doped InAs layer scatters TE-polarized light into near fields with components perpendicular to the magnetic field, allowing the magneto-optic response of the InAs to act on them. Under a 0.48 T field from a permanent Halbach array, this structure exhibits a difference in absorptivity between $+B$ and $-B$ of 0.035 in both TE and TM polarization at 16.6 $\mu$m. Our approach shows that the magneto-optic response of a planar semiconductor and the resonances of a dielectric metasurface can be designed together, offering a potential route to dual-polarization nonreciprocity at fields available from permanent magnets for emerging energy and heat transfer technologies.
item.dc:creator: Mason Christiansen, Jae S. Hwang, Yi Jie Lin, Aryan Zaveri, Tianjun Li, Daniel Cui, Baolai Liang, Aaswath P. Raman

item.title: Disentangling Spin and Orbital Contributions in the Search for Altermagnetic Terahertz Conversion in RuO2
item.description: arXiv:2611.09098v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Rutile RuO2 has emerged as a prominent candidate altermagnet, yet the microscopic origin of its reported charge-angular-momentum conversion remains unsettled. Recent theoretical and experimental advances have highlighted a potentially dominant role of orbital transport, raising a fundamental ambiguity between spin- and orbital-mediated conversion in RuO2. Here, we report the first experimental disentanglement of the spin- and orbital-to-charge conversion channels in RuO2 heterostructures using terahertz emission spectroscopy. We identify Fe as a predominantly spin-current injector, whereas Ni and permalloy predominantly inject orbital currents, revealing a substantial orbital contribution to ultrafast terahertz emission. Under controlled spin-current injection, we find no evidence for inverse altermagnetic spin-splitting effect. Instead, the observed anisotropy is consistent with an anisotropic inverse spin Hall response that is strongly conditioned by the near-interface environment. Under orbital-current injection, the anisotropy is markedly weaker, indicating that orbital-to-charge conversion is largely isotropic in RuO2. Our results establish orbital transport and interface-conditioned spin Hall conversion as key to terahertz emission from RuO2, underscoring the need to disentangle spin, orbital, and interfacial contributions before assigning anisotropy to altermagnetism.
item.dc:creator: Jiahao Liu, Yuxiao Mo, Tongyang Guan, Wenhui Fang, Yongwei Cui, Wentao Qin, Zhe Yuan, Lishu Zhang, Zhensheng Tao, Yizheng Wu

item.title: Scanning Probe Control, Quantum Dynamics, and Dispersive Readout of Suspended Carbon Nanotube Resonators
item.description: arXiv:2611.09581v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Suspended carbon nanotubes (CNTs) offer promising opportunities for quantum nanomechanics owing to their small effective mass, strong electrostatic tunability, and mechanical nonlinearity. We develop a unified theoretical framework for coherent control and readout of a suspended CNT driven by an atomic force microscope (AFM) tip and capacitively coupled to a Cooper-pair box (CPB). We first derive the linear and nonlinear Duffing response of the CNT and quantify the effects of AFM force gradients, tip-position fluctuations, and voltage noise on mechanical stability, dephasing, and heating. These results establish operating conditions for coherent actuation with limited backaction. We then quantize the Duffing oscillator, derive its Kerr anharmonicity, and identify the requirements for selective control of individual vibrational transitions. Estimates of thermal occupation and active cooling illustrate the constraints for CNT modes spanning frequencies from 54 MHz to 5.37 GHz. Finally, we derive the CNT--CPB interaction and its dispersive limit, showing how phonon number and parity can be mapped onto the CPB through Ramsey interferometry and detected using quantum-capacitance readout. The resulting framework identifies the conditions under which localized AFM actuation, nonlinear quantum dynamics, and superconducting state-resolved detection can operate within a single CNT device.
item.dc:creator: Cristian Staii

item.title: Layer-Peeling Inversion of Temporal Refractive Index Profiles from Noisy Data
item.description: arXiv:2611.09630v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce a direct method for reconstructing the temporal evolution of a medium from electromagnetic field measurements. A sequence of temporal refractive-index changes splits an incident wave into forward- and backward-propagating components, producing a \emph{spatial} response of finite extent. We show that this finite support, together with causality, enables sequential reconstruction of the temporal interfaces through a time-domain extension of layer peeling. For continuously varying media, we introduce a time-adjusted Goupillaud medium and, through space-time duality, establish the corresponding momentum-conservation and admissibility conditions. The method remains robust under incomplete and noisy measurements, providing a general framework for the metrology, characterization, and design of time-varying electromagnetic systems.
item.dc:creator: Ohad Silbiger, Yakir Hadad

item.title: Inversion symmetry breaking by interlayer hybridization in a tetralayer van der Waals heterostructure
item.description: arXiv:2611.09669v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Inversion symmetry breaking unlocks a broad range of physical phenomena fundamental for modern technologies, motivating efforts to engineer noncentrosymmetric materials. In this context, monolayer transition metal dichalcogenides, which naturally lack inversion symmetry, have emerged as a versatile platform for valley physics, strong excitonic effects, and nonlinear optics. However, in their hexagonal stacking phase, inversion symmetry is restored in even-layer stacks and bulk form, suppressing these effects and limiting applications. In this work, inversion symmetry breaking is demonstrated in a vertically stacked tetralayer heterostructure assembled from two intrinsically centrosymmetric bilayer flakes, as evidenced by second harmonic generation measurements with an intensity comparable to that of their constituent monolayer. Spectroscopic measurements and theoretical estimations indicate that effective symmetry breaking in the tetralayer heterostructure is driven by interlayer hybridization, giving rise to pronounced electronic and phononic signatures. This symmetry breaking further induces polar anisotropy, with an intensity ratio reaching 2.36. We propose that asymmetric contributions from excitons to the second harmonic optical dipole may influence this behavior. These findings establish interlayer coupling as a critical mechanism for introducing inversion symmetry breaking and tuning the optical response of van der Waals heterostructures, providing a powerful strategy for photonics and optoelectronics in two-dimensional materials.

item.title: Controlled spin-torque driven domain wall motion using staggered magnetic nanowires
item.description: arXiv:1908.09304v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The growing demand for storage, due to big data applications, cannot be met by hard disk drives. Domain wall (DW) memory devices such as racetrack memory offer an alternative route to achieve high capacity storage. In DW memory, control of domain wall positions and their motion using spin-transfer torque are important challenges. In this paper, we demonstrate controlled domain wall motion using spin-transfer torque in staggered magnetic nanowires. The devices, fabricated using electron-beam lithography, were tested using a magneto-optical Kerr microscopy and electrical transport measurements. The depinning current, pinning potential and thermal stability were found to depend on the device dimensions of the staggering nanowires. Thus, the proposed staggering configuration helps to fine-tune the properties of domain wall devices for memory applications.
item.dc:creator: H. Mohammed, S. Al Risi, T. L. Jin, J. Kosel, S. N. Piramanayagam, R. Sbiaa

item.title: On the Role of Color Temperature and Color Rendering Index of White-Light LEDs on the Theoretical Efficiency Limit of Indoor Photovoltaics
item.description: arXiv:2506.20811v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: As the Internet of Things (IoT) continues to grow, the demand for sustainable indoor power sources is increasing. Indoor photovoltaics (IPVs), which are currently in development, present a renewable solution but must be designed to match specific light sources to maximize efficiency. While previous studies have emphasized the role of white-light LED correlated color temperature (CCT) in determining IPV efficiency and optimum bandgap energy, the role of color rendering index (CRI) remains less understood. In this study, we employ detailed-balance calculations to assess the theoretical maximum efficiency and optimal bandgap energies of IPVs under commercial white-light LED illumination varying in both CCT (2200 K to 6500 K) and CRI (70, 80, and 90). Our results confirm that lower CCTs yield higher efficiencies and lower optimal bandgaps; however, contrary to prior assumptions that CRI has negligible impact on IPV material choice and performance, we demonstrate that commercial high-CRI LEDs, where said high CRI was achieved by extending the emission into the red, can necessitate the use of materials with significantly lower bandgap energies for optimum efficiency. We also evaluate the performance of various IPVs at fixed bandgaps, revealing that while optimal IPV performance is achieved with wide-bandgap materials under lower CRI lighting, mature technologies like silicon and CdTe can benefit from high-CRI illumination. These findings underscore the need to consider color characteristics beyond CCT when evaluating solar cells for indoor IoT applications.
item.dc:creator: Aditi Sharma, Ian Yum, Alexander A. Guaman, Gavin A. Akmam, Jason A. R\"ohr
